editorial:
James is a rich hedge fund guy who suddenly gets ten years in San Quentin for fraud he swears he didn't commit. With only a month to prepare, he hires Darnell, a hardworking car wash owner who has never broken the law, to teach him how to survive behind bars. The joke is that James assumes Darnell must have prison experience simply because he is Black, which sets up a steady stream of awkward, uncomfortable, and often hilarious moments as the two men clash and slowly bond.

The movie leans hard on the chemistry between Will Ferrell and Kevin Hart, and that is where it shines brightest. Their back-and-forth energy keeps even the weaker jokes moving, and a few scenes, like the prison yard training and the gang meeting, land big laughs. The humor can be crude and sometimes leans on stereotypes, which may turn off some viewers, but if you enjoy raunchy buddy comedies, this one delivers. It is a fun pick for a relaxed movie night, and you can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final act, James and Darnell dig into the case and discover that James's boss Martin framed him for the fraud. They crash Martin's fancy party, expose the evidence in front of everyone, and clear James's name. Martin is arrested, James is freed, and Darnell earns a big reward that helps his family. The two part as genuine friends, having learned to drop their assumptions about each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves raunchy buddy comedies and Will Ferrell or Kevin Hart movies.
